memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The allotment for Joseph began at the Jordan, east of the springs of Jericho, and went up from there through the desert into the hill country of Bethel. It went on from Bethel (that is, Luz), crossed over to the territory of the Arkites in Ataroth, descended westward to the territory of the Japhletites as far as the region of Lower Beth Horon and to Gezer, ending at the Mediterranean Sea - Josh 16:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The inheritance now passes to the descendants of Joseph. It is worth pausing on that name. Joseph was the brother sold into slavery, wrongly imprisoned, forgotten in a foreign land. Yet here, generations later, his family receives a rich portion in the Promised Land — hill country, towns, territory stretching to the sea. The story that began in a pit ends in an inheritance.

Remember what Joseph himself said to the brothers who had wronged him: "You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good" (Gen 50:20). The suffering of one man became the saving of many, and now his descendants inherit a home in the land of promise. God's faithfulness reached across the betrayal, the slavery, the prison, and the long years, to keep His word to Joseph's line.

This is a quiet encouragement for anyone whose story has held real hardship. God's purposes are not derailed by the wrongs done to us or the pits we have been thrown into. The same God who turned Joseph's suffering into blessing is weaving His good purposes through our hardships too (Rom 8:28). What looks like the end of hope may be the hidden beginning of an inheritance. The God of Joseph is faithful across the generations, and He is faithful still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has hardship ever made you feel God's purposes for you were derailed?
- How does Joseph's story encourage you that God's faithfulness outlasts our pits?
- Where might God be turning past harm into future good in your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your purposes are not derailed by the wrongs done to me or the hard places I have been. Like Joseph, help me trust that You work all things for good. Amen.
